rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH txn AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
customer_ranges AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', MIN(txn_date))) AS min_month_start,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', MAX(txn_date))) AS max_month_start
  FROM txn
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
months_expanded AS (
  SELECT
    cr.customer_id,
    cr.min_month_start AS month_start,
    date(cr.min_month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', cr.min_month_start) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', cr.min_month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month_number,
    cr.max_month_start
  FROM customer_ranges cr
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    me.customer_id,
    date(me.month_start, '+1 month') AS month_start,
    date(date(me.month_start, '+1 month'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(me.month_start, '+1 month')) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(me.month_start, '+1 month')) AS INTEGER) AS month_number,
    me.max_month_start
  FROM months_expanded me
  WHERE date(me.month_start, '+1 month') <= me.max_month_start
),
monthly_txn AS (
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.month_start,
    m.month_end,
    m.calendar_year,
    m.month_number,
    IFNULL(SUM(t.txn_amount), 0) AS month_total
  FROM months_expanded m
  LEFT JOIN txn t
    ON t.customer_id = m.customer_id
    AND date(t.txn_date) BETWEEN m.month_start AND m.month_end
  GROUP BY m.customer_id, m.month_start, m.month_end, m.calendar_year, m.month_number
),
closing_balances AS (
  SELECT
    mt.customer_id,
    mt.month_start,
    mt.month_end,
    mt.calendar_year,
    mt.month_number,
    mt.month_total,
    (SELECT SUM(mt2.month_total)
     FROM monthly_txn mt2
     WHERE mt2.customer_id = mt.customer_id
       AND (mt2.calendar_year < mt.calendar_year
            OR (mt2.calendar_year = mt.calendar_year AND mt2.month_number <= mt.month_number))
    ) AS closing_balance
  FROM monthly_txn mt
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  month_start AS month_start_date,
  month_end AS month_end_date,
  calendar_year,
  month_number,
  closing_balance AS closing_balance,
  (closing_balance - (
     SELECT cb_prev.closing_balance
     FROM closing_balances cb_prev
     WHERE cb_prev.customer_id = cb.customer_id
       AND (cb_prev.calendar_year < cb.calendar_year
            OR (cb_prev.calendar_year = cb.calendar_year AND cb_prev.month_number < cb.month_number))
     ORDER BY cb_prev.calendar_year DESC, cb_prev.month_number DESC
     LIMIT 1
  )) AS monthly_change,
  closing_balance AS cumulative_balance
FROM closing_balances cb
ORDER BY customer_id ASC, calendar_year ASC, month_number ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH distinct_customers_2020 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE date(txn_date) BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
),
customer_transactions_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    CAST(txn_amount AS REAL) AS txn_amount,
    lower(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_month
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE date(txn_date) BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
),
customer_monthly_balances AS (
  -- balances per customer per month (only months where they had transactions)
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    ct.calendar_year,
    ct.calendar_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN 0 ELSE ct.txn_amount END) AS sum_withdrawals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE -ct.txn_amount END) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customer_transactions_normalized ct
  WHERE ct.calendar_year = 2020
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, ct.calendar_year, ct.calendar_month
),
months AS (
  SELECT 2020 AS calendar_year, 1 AS calendar_month UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,2 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,3 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,4 UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,5 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,6 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,7 UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,8 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,9 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,10 UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,11 UNION ALL SELECT 2020,12
),
stats_per_month AS (
  -- for every customer (present anywhere in 2020) and every month, treat missing as 0
  SELECT
    m.calendar_month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(b.month_end_balance, 0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(b.month_end_balance, 0)) AS avg_month_end_balance
  FROM distinct_customers_2020 c
  CROSS JOIN months m
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balances b
    ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id
   AND b.calendar_year = m.calendar_year
   AND b.calendar_month = m.calendar_month
  GROUP BY m.calendar_month
),
ranked_desc AS (
  SELECT
    calendar_month,
    positive_count,
    avg_month_end_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count DESC, calendar_month ASC) AS rn_desc
  FROM stats_per_month
),
ranked_asc AS (
  SELECT
    calendar_month,
    positive_count,
    avg_month_end_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_count ASC, calendar_month ASC) AS rn_asc
  FROM stats_per_month
)
SELECT
  printf('2020-%02d', best.calendar_month) AS best_month,
  best.positive_count AS best_month_positive_customer_count,
  best.avg_month_end_balance AS best_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  printf('2020-%02d', worst.calendar_month) AS worst_month,
  worst.positive_count AS worst_month_positive_customer_count,
  worst.avg_month_end_balance AS worst_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  (best.avg_month_end_balance - worst.avg_month_end_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (SELECT calendar_month, positive_count, avg_month_end_balance FROM ranked_desc WHERE rn_desc = 1) AS best,
  (SELECT calendar_month, positive_count, avg_month_end_balance FROM ranked_asc WHERE rn_asc = 1) AS worst
LIMIT 1

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    LOWER(txn_type) AS txn_type,
    txn_amount,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE LOWER(txn_type) IN ('deposit','withdrawal')
),
customer_monthly_net AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    -- canonical month bucket as 'YYYY-MM-01'
    (strftime('%Y', txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', txn_date) || '-01') AS month_bucket_date,
    txn_year AS year,
    txn_month AS month,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
           WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
           ELSE 0 END
    ) AS monthly_net
  FROM customer_transaction_canonical
  GROUP BY customer_id, year, month, month_bucket_date
),
customer_monthly_closing_balance AS (
  SELECT
    cmn.customer_id,
    cmn.month_bucket_date,
    cmn.year,
    cmn.month,
    cmn.monthly_net,
    -- cumulative sum up to this month (inclusive)
    (
      SELECT COALESCE(SUM(m2.monthly_net), 0)
      FROM customer_monthly_net m2
      WHERE m2.customer_id = cmn.customer_id
        AND (m2.year < cmn.year OR (m2.year = cmn.year AND m2.month <= cmn.month))
    ) AS closing_balance,
    -- cumulative sum up to prior month (exclusive)
    (
      SELECT COALESCE(SUM(m3.monthly_net), 0)
      FROM customer_monthly_net m3
      WHERE m3.customer_id = cmn.customer_id
        AND (m3.year < cmn.year OR (m3.year = cmn.year AND m3.month < cmn.month))
    ) AS prior_month_closing_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_net cmn
),
latest_per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    closing_balance,
    prior_month_closing_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY year DESC, month DESC) AS rn
  FROM customer_monthly_closing_balance
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_with_growth_gt_5_percent
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    closing_balance,
    prior_month_closing_balance,
    CASE
      WHEN prior_month_closing_balance = 0 THEN closing_balance * 100.0
      ELSE (closing_balance - prior_month_closing_balance) * 1.0 / prior_month_closing_balance
    END AS growth_rate
  FROM latest_per_customer
  WHERE rn = 1
) t

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT substr(txn_date,1,7) AS month_ym
  FROM customer_transactions
),
ordered_months AS (
  SELECT month_ym,
         date(month_ym || '-01') AS month_first_day,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY month_ym) AS rn
  FROM months
),
cutoffs AS (
  -- for each month starting from the second distinct month, cutoff = day before month_first_day
  SELECT o.month_ym,
         o.month_first_day,
         date(o.month_first_day, '-1 day') AS cutoff_date
  FROM ordered_months o
  WHERE o.rn > 1
),
distinct_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
-- compute each customer's cumulative balance up to each cutoff_date (including customers with no txns => 0)
customer_balances AS (
  SELECT
    c.month_ym AS month,
    cust.customer_id,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(ct.txn_amount)
      FROM customer_transactions ct
      WHERE ct.customer_id = cust.customer_id
        AND ct.txn_date <= c.cutoff_date
    ), 0) AS balance_up_to_cutoff
  FROM distinct_customers cust
  CROSS JOIN cutoffs c
),
final_per_month AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN balance_up_to_cutoff < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance_up_to_cutoff END) AS total_balance_previous_month
  FROM customer_balances
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month || '-01' AS month, total_balance_previous_month
FROM final_per_month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_daily_net_change AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(substr(txn_date, 1, 10)) AS date,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      ELSE -txn_amount
    END
  ) AS daily_net_change
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, date(substr(txn_date, 1, 10))
),
customer_daily_eod_balance AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.date,
  -- running end-of-day balance: cumulative sum of daily_net_change per customer ordered by date
  (SELECT SUM(d2.daily_net_change)
   FROM customer_daily_net_change d2
   WHERE d2.customer_id = d.customer_id
     AND date(d2.date) <= date(d.date)
  ) AS end_of_day_balance,
  -- flag if the date is in the same month as the customer's first transaction month
  (CASE
     WHEN strftime('%Y-%m', d.date) = strftime('%Y-%m', (
         SELECT MIN(date) FROM customer_daily_net_change d3 WHERE d3.customer_id = d.customer_id
     )) THEN 1 ELSE 0
   END) AS is_first_txn_month
FROM customer_daily_net_change d
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id AS customer_id,
  d.date AS date,
  substr(d.date,1,7) AS month,
  AVG(d.end_of_day_balance) OVER (
    PARTITION BY d.customer_id
    ORDER BY d.date
    ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS rolling_30day_avg_balance,
  CASE
    WHEN substr(d.date,1,7) = substr(min(d.date) OVER (PARTITION BY d.customer_id),1,7) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS baseline_month
FROM customer_daily_eod_balance d
WHERE d.end_of_day_balance IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    -- ensure there are at least 30 consecutive days ending on d.date for this customer:
    -- require that the count of distinct dates in the 30-day window equals 30
    (SELECT COUNT(1)
     FROM customer_daily_eod_balance x
     WHERE x.customer_id = d.customer_id
       AND x.date <= d.date
       AND x.date > date(d.date, '-30 days')
    ) = 30
)
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN monthly_max < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE monthly_max END) AS monthly_total_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month,
    MAX(rolling_30day_avg_balance) AS monthly_max
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance
  WHERE month <> baseline_month
  GROUP BY customer_id, month
) per_cust_month
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- per-customer min/max txn date
cust_ranges AS (
  SELECT customer_id, DATE(MIN(txn_date)) AS min_dt, DATE(MAX(txn_date)) AS max_dt
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- digit table 0..9999 to generate date ranges (4-digit cross join)
digits AS (
  SELECT (a.n + b.n*10 + c.n*100 + d.n*1000) AS n
  FROM (SELECT 0 n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) a,
       (SELECT 0 n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) b,
       (SELECT 0 n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9) c,
       (SELECT 0 n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4) d
),
-- generate one row per customer per date between their min and max txn date
cust_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    cr.customer_id,
    DATE(cr.min_dt, '+' || d.n || ' days') AS calendar_date
  FROM cust_ranges cr
  JOIN digits d ON DATE(cr.min_dt, '+' || d.n || ' days') <= cr.max_dt
),
-- cumulative balance per customer per date: sum of txn_amounts up to that date
cust_daily_bal AS (
  SELECT
    cc.customer_id,
    cc.calendar_date,
    COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(txn_amount) FROM customer_transactions t
      WHERE t.customer_id = cc.customer_id
        AND DATE(t.txn_date) <= cc.calendar_date
    ), 0) AS raw_balance
  FROM cust_calendar cc
),
-- treat negatives as zero
cust_daily_bal_nonneg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    calendar_date,
    CASE WHEN raw_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE raw_balance END AS balance
  FROM cust_daily_bal
),
-- per customer per month max daily balance
cust_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    STRFTIME('%Y-%m', calendar_date) AS month,
    MAX(balance) AS customer_month_max
  FROM cust_daily_bal_nonneg
  GROUP BY customer_id, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', calendar_date)
)
-- final: sum across customers per month
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(customer_month_max) AS monthly_total_max_balances
FROM cust_month_max
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH shopping_cart_pages_with_product AS (
  SELECT page_id, page_name, product_id
  FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
  WHERE product_id IS NOT NULL
    AND page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
),
event_type_names AS (
  SELECT event_type, event_name
  FROM shopping_cart_event_identifier
),
events_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    e.visit_id,
    e.cookie_id,
    e.page_id,
    p.product_id,
    p.page_name,
    e.event_type,
    et.event_name,
    e.sequence_number,
    e.event_time
  FROM shopping_cart_events e
  JOIN shopping_cart_pages_with_product p
    ON e.page_id = p.page_id
  LEFT JOIN event_type_names et
    ON e.event_type = et.event_type
  WHERE e.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
),
-- Precompute purchases per cookie_id and product_id with their event_time for efficient lookup
purchases AS (
  SELECT cookie_id, product_id, event_time
  FROM events_enriched
  WHERE event_name = 'Purchase'
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name AS product_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS page_views_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS add_to_cart_count,
  -- abandoned_in_cart_count: count of Add-to-Cart events for which there is no later Purchase by same cookie_id for same product_id
  COALESCE(SUM(
    CASE 
      WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM purchases pu
          WHERE pu.cookie_id = e.cookie_id
            AND pu.product_id = e.product_id
            AND pu.event_time > e.event_time
        ) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
      ELSE 0
    END
  ), 0) AS abandoned_in_cart_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS purchase_count
FROM shopping_cart_pages_with_product p
LEFT JOIN events_enriched e
  ON e.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.page_name
HAVING
  (SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL AND SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0)
  OR (SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL AND SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0)
  OR (SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL AND SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0)
ORDER BY page_views_count DESC, p.product_id ASC

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH interest_map_id_name AS (
  SELECT
    id AS interest_id,
    interest_name
  FROM interest_map
),
interest_monthly_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    interest_id,
    CAST(_year AS INTEGER) AS yr,
    CAST(_month AS INTEGER) AS mon,
    printf('%04d-%02d-01', CAST(_year AS INTEGER), CAST(_month AS INTEGER)) AS month_date,
    composition,
    index_value,
    (composition / NULLIF(index_value, 0.0)) AS composition_index_ratio
  FROM interest_metrics
  WHERE _year IS NOT NULL
    AND _month IS NOT NULL
    -- restrict to months between 09-2018 and 08-2019 inclusive
    AND (
      (_year = 2018 AND _month >= 9)
      OR (_year = 2019 AND _month <= 8)
    )
    -- exclude null or zero index_value to avoid division by zero (NULLIF handled but also exclude NULL)
    AND index_value IS NOT NULL
),
monthly_max_ratio AS (
  SELECT
    imm.month_date AS month_date,
    MAX(imm.composition_index_ratio) AS max_ratio
  FROM interest_monthly_metrics imm
  GROUP BY imm.month_date
),
monthly_top AS (
  -- pick the single interest per month with the max ratio; break ties by smallest interest_id
  SELECT m.month_date AS month_date,
         m.interest_id AS interest_id,
         m.composition_index_ratio AS composition_index_ratio
  FROM interest_monthly_metrics m
  JOIN monthly_max_ratio mx ON mx.month_date = m.month_date AND mx.max_ratio = m.composition_index_ratio
  JOIN (
    SELECT mm.month_date AS month_date, MIN(mm.interest_id) AS min_id
    FROM interest_monthly_metrics mm
    JOIN monthly_max_ratio mx2 ON mx2.month_date = mm.month_date AND mx2.max_ratio = mm.composition_index_ratio
    GROUP BY mm.month_date
  ) tie ON tie.month_date = m.month_date AND tie.min_id = m.interest_id
),
monthly_top_named AS (
  SELECT
    mt.month_date AS month_date,
    mt.interest_id AS interest_id,
    imn.interest_name AS interest_name,
    mt.composition_index_ratio AS max_index_composition
  FROM monthly_top mt
  LEFT JOIN interest_map_id_name imn ON imn.interest_id = mt.interest_id
),
months_range AS (
  SELECT date('2018-09-01') AS start_date, date('2019-08-01') AS end_date
),
rolling_3mo AS (
  SELECT
    cur.month_date AS month_date,
    (SELECT AVG(m2.max_index_composition)
     FROM monthly_top_named m2
     WHERE m2.month_date IN (
       date(cur.month_date, '-2 months'),
       date(cur.month_date, '-1 month'),
       cur.month_date
     )
    ) AS rolling_avg_3mo,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM monthly_top_named m2
     WHERE m2.month_date IN (
       date(cur.month_date, '-2 months'),
       date(cur.month_date, '-1 month'),
       cur.month_date
     )
    ) AS months_count_in_window
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT month_date FROM monthly_top_named
  ) cur
  WHERE cur.month_date BETWEEN (SELECT start_date FROM months_range) AND (SELECT end_date FROM months_range)
)
SELECT
  cur.month_date AS date,
  cur.interest_name AS interest_name,
  ROUND(cur.max_index_composition, 6) AS max_index_composition,
  CASE WHEN r.months_count_in_window = 3 THEN ROUND(r.rolling_avg_3mo, 6) ELSE NULL END AS rolling_avg_3mo,
  prev1.interest_name AS prev_month_interest_name,
  ROUND(prev1.max_index_composition, 6) AS prev_month_max_index_composition,
  prev2.interest_name AS prev_2_month_interest_name,
  ROUND(prev2.max_index_composition, 6) AS prev_2_month_max_index_composition

    (
      SELECT DISTINCT order_id, seller_id
      FROM order_items_enriched
    ) AS oi_seller
  LEFT JOIN order_metrics
    ON oi_seller.order_id = order_metrics.order_id
  GROUP BY oi_seller.seller_id
),
-- top product category (english) per seller by item count
top_cat AS (
  SELECT product_by_seller.seller_id, product_category_translation_map.product_category_name_english
  FROM
    (
      SELECT
        seller_id,
        product_category_name,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, product_category_name) AS rn
      FROM order_items_enriched
      GROUP BY seller_id, product_category_name
    ) AS product_by_seller
  LEFT JOIN product_category_translation_map
    ON product_by_seller.product_category_name = product_category_translation_map.product_category_name
  WHERE product_by_seller.rn = 1
)
SELECT
  s_agg.seller_id,
  s_agg.total_sales_revenue,
  s_agg.total_items_sold,
  s_agg.average_item_price,
  o_metrics.average_review_score,
  o_metrics.average_packing_time_hours,
  top_cat.product_category_name_english AS top_product_category_name_english
FROM s_agg
LEFT JOIN o_metrics
  ON s_agg.seller_id = o_metrics.seller_id
LEFT JOIN top_cat
  ON s_agg.seller_id = top_cat.seller_id
WHERE s_agg.total_items_sold > 100
ORDER BY s_agg.total_sales_revenue DESC
